# understand-repo

When you need to understand this repository — its architecture, module layout,
technologies, APIs, database schema, or feature ownership — **read the
repo-mapper documentation first**. It is a structured, always-up-to-date map
of the entire codebase generated by
[repo-mapper](https://github.com/anushibinj/repo-mapper).

## Step 1 — Read the entrypoint

Open `.repo-mapper/README.md`. It contains:

- **Snapshot** — current branch and commit
- **Languages** — every language and its file count
- **Modules** — detected sub-modules (frontend, backend, etc.)
- **Contents** — links to all detailed views

Read this file **before** opening any source file.

## Step 2 — Follow the links for the area you care about

| You want to know about… | Read this file |
|---|---|
| High-level system layers / diagrams | `.repo-mapper/architecture.md` |
| Controllers, services, repositories, APIs | `.repo-mapper/backend.md` |
| Pages, components, hooks, routes | `.repo-mapper/frontend.md` |
| Tables, columns, foreign keys | `.repo-mapper/database.md` |
| Cross-cutting feature ownership | `.repo-mapper/features.md` |
| Full machine-readable model | `.repo-mapper/repo-map.json` |
| System / ER diagrams (Mermaid) | `.repo-mapper/diagrams` |

## Step 3 — Open source files only for implementation details

Once you know *where* something lives from the map, open only the specific
source file you need. Do not crawl the repository tree looking for context —
the map already provides it.

## When the map does not exist

If `.repo-mapper/README.md` is missing, the repository has not been scanned
yet. Ask the user to run:

```bash
repo-mapper scan
```

This will generate the full documentation set in `.repo-mapper`.
